Primary.text: What is the plural of "engine"?
Primary.explanation: Most nouns just add "s" to make the plural.

Primary.text: What is the plural of "child"?
Primary.explanation: "Child" has a special plural: "children".

Primary.text: What is the plural of "lorry"?
Primary.explanation: When a word ends in a consonant and "y", change the "y" to "ies".

Primary.text: What is the plural of "mouse"?
Primary.explanation: "Mouse" has a special plural: "mice".

Primary.text: What is the opposite of "happy"?
Primary.explanation: "Sad" means the opposite of "happy".

Primary.text: What is the opposite of "heavy"?
Primary.explanation: Something that is not heavy is light.

Primary.text: What is the opposite of "early"?
Primary.explanation: If Thomas is not early, he is late.

Primary.text: Which word means the same as "small"?
Primary.explanation: "Small" and "little" have the same meaning.

Primary.text: Which word means the same as "quick"?
Primary.explanation: "Quick" and "fast" both mean moving at speed.

Primary.text: Which word rhymes with "coal"?
Primary.explanation: "Coal" and "hole" end with the same sound.

Primary.text: Which word rhymes with "track"?
Primary.explanation: "Track" and "back" both end with "-ack".

Primary.text: Which word should always start with a capital letter?
Primary.explanation: Days of the week always start with a capital letter: Monday.

Primary.text: Which sentence has a capital letter and a full stop in the right places?
Primary.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

Primary.text: Which punctuation mark should end this sentence: "Can Toby come to the quarry"
Primary.explanation: The sentence asks something, so it needs a question mark.

Primary.text: What is the past tense of "stop"?
Primary.explanation: Double the "p" and add "ed" to get "stopped".

Primary.text: Which word completes the sentence: "Yesterday Percy ____ a cow on the line."
Primary.explanation: "Saw" is the past tense of "see".

Primary.text: What is the past tense of "whistle"?
Primary.explanation: Words ending in "e" just add "d" for the past tense.

Primary.text: What is the short form (contraction) of "do not"?
Primary.explanation: The apostrophe in "don't" shows where the "o" of "not" was left out.

Primary.text: What does "can't" mean?
Primary.explanation: "Can't" is the short form of "cannot".

Primary.text: What is the short form (contraction) of "it is"?
Primary.explanation: "It's" means "it is"; the apostrophe replaces the "i".

Primary.text: Which name comes first in alphabetical order?
Primary.explanation: "E" comes before "H", "P" and "T" in the alphabet.

Primary.text: Which list is in alphabetical order?
Primary.explanation: E, G, J, T follow the order of the alphabet.

Primary.text: Which name comes last in alphabetical order?
Primary.explanation: Look at the second letter: a, i, o, u, so "Duck" comes last.

Primary.text: Which is the correct spelling of the place where trains stop?
Primary.explanation: "Station" ends with the letters "tion".

Primary.text: Which is the correct spelling?
Primary.explanation: "Whistle" has a silent "h" and a silent "t".

Primary.text: Which is the correct spelling of a person you like to play with?
Primary.explanation: Remember: a "friend" is there to the "end".

Primary.text: Which word is a noun in the sentence "The crane lifted the heavy box."?
Primary.explanation: "Crane" names a thing, so it is a noun.

Primary.text: Which word is a verb in the sentence "Percy pushed the trucks."?
Primary.explanation: "Pushed" is the action, so it is a verb.

Primary.text: Which word is an adjective in the sentence "Gordon is a big engine."?
Primary.explanation: "Big" describes Gordon, so it is an adjective.

Primary.text: Which word best joins the sentence: "Thomas was tired ____ he kept going."
Primary.explanation: "But" joins two ideas that contrast with each other.

Primary.text: Which of these is a compound word (two words joined together)?
Primary.explanation: "Railway" is made from "rail" and "way".

Primary.text: How many syllables are in the name "Harvey"?
Primary.explanation: Har-vey has two beats, so it has two syllables.

Primary.text: Which letter is a vowel?
Primary.explanation: The vowels are a, e, i, o and u.

Primary.text: Which word starts with the same sound as "Percy"?
Primary.explanation: "Percy" and "pig" both start with a "p" sound.

Primary.text: Which sentence needs a question mark at the end?
Primary.explanation: It asks a question, so it needs a question mark.

Primary.text: Which sentence should end with an exclamation mark?
Primary.explanation: A sudden warning or shout ends with an exclamation mark.

Primary.text: What is the opposite of "empty"?
Primary.explanation: A truck that is not empty is full.

Primary.text: Which word means the same as "shout"?
Primary.explanation: "Shout" and "yell" both mean to call out loudly.

Primary.text: Which word means more than one?
Primary.explanation: The "s" on the end of "trucks" shows there is more than one.

Primary.text: Which of these is the name of a place (a proper noun)?
Primary.explanation: Knapford is the name of a special place, so it starts with a capital letter.

Secondary.text: Which word is a pronoun in the sentence "Emily said she would help."?
Secondary.explanation: "She" takes the place of the noun "Emily".

Secondary.text: Which word is a preposition in the sentence "Toby waited under the bridge."?
Secondary.explanation: "Under" shows the position of Toby in relation to the bridge.

Secondary.text: Which word is a conjunction in the sentence "Percy was late because the signal was red."?
Secondary.explanation: "Because" joins the two clauses together.

Secondary.text: Which word is an adverb in the sentence "Tomorrow Henry will visit Wellsworth."?
Secondary.explanation: "Tomorrow" tells us when the action happens, so it is an adverb.

Secondary.text: Which phrase correctly shows the sheds belonging to several engines?
Secondary.explanation: For a plural ending in "s", the apostrophe goes after the "s".

Secondary.text: Which word completes the sentence: "The engine blew ____ whistle."
Secondary.explanation: "Its" shows possession; "it's" means "it is".

Secondary.text: Which word completes the sentence: "Thomas and Percy parked ____ trucks in the yard."
Secondary.explanation: "Their" shows that the trucks belong to Thomas and Percy.

Secondary.text: Which word completes the sentence: "____ going to Vicarstown tomorrow."
Secondary.explanation: "They're" is short for "they are".

Secondary.text: Which word completes the sentence: "Gordon was ____ proud to pull the trucks."
Secondary.explanation: "Too" means "excessively" or "also".

Secondary.text: Which word completes the sentence: "The engines had to ____ at the red signal."
Secondary.explanation: "Wait" means to stay; "weight" means how heavy something is.

Secondary.text: What does the prefix "un-" mean in the word "unhappy"?
Secondary.explanation: "Unhappy" means "not happy".

Secondary.text: What does the prefix "re-" mean in the word "rebuild"?
Secondary.explanation: To rebuild is to build again.

Secondary.text: What does the suffix "-less" mean in the word "fearless"?
Secondary.explanation: "Fearless" means without fear.

Secondary.text: Which suffix turns the verb "enjoy" into a noun?
Secondary.explanation: "Enjoyment" is a noun; "enjoyable" is an adjective.

Secondary.text: Which sentence contains a simile?
options: Thomas was as busy as a bee.
Secondary.correctAnswer: Thomas was as busy as a bee.
Secondary.explanation: A simile compares two things using "as" or "like".

Secondary.text: Which figure of speech is used in "The sun smiled down on Knapford Station."?
Secondary.explanation: Giving the sun a human action (smiling) is personification.

Secondary.text: Which figure of speech is used in "Percy puffed past the purple post box."?
Secondary.explanation: Repeating the same starting sound ("p") is alliteration.

Secondary.text: Which word is an example of onomatopoeia?
Secondary.explanation: "Clang" sounds like the noise it describes.

Secondary.text: Which figure of speech is used in "Gordon said the trucks weighed a million tonnes."?
Secondary.explanation: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for effect.

Secondary.text: Which sentence is the passive form of "Harvey lifted the crate."?
options: The crate was lifted by Harvey.
Secondary.correctAnswer: The crate was lifted by Harvey.
Secondary.explanation: In the passive voice, the object becomes the subject and "by" names the doer.

Secondary.text: Which verb correctly completes the sentence: "Each of the engines ____ its own shed."
Secondary.explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "has".

Secondary.text: Which verb correctly completes the sentence: "The trucks in the siding ____ full of coal."
Secondary.explanation: The subject "trucks" is plural, so it takes "are".

Secondary.text: Which tense is used in "Emily will have delivered the mail by noon."?
Secondary.explanation: "Will have" plus a past participle forms the future perfect.

Secondary.text: Which tense is used in "James was polishing his buffers."?
Secondary.explanation: "Was" plus an "-ing" verb forms the past continuous.

Secondary.text: What is the main clause in "Although it was raining, Edward finished his journey."?
Secondary.explanation: The main clause makes sense on its own as a sentence.

Secondary.text: What type of sentence is "Thomas stopped, and Percy waited."?
Secondary.explanation: Two main clauses joined by "and" make a compound sentence.

Secondary.text: What does the root "tele" mean in the word "telescope"?
Secondary.explanation: "Tele" comes from Greek and means "far", as in telephone and television.

Secondary.text: What does the root "port" mean in the word "transport"?
Secondary.explanation: "Port" comes from Latin "portare", meaning "to carry".

Secondary.text: What does "reluctant" mean in "Diesel was reluctant to help."?
Secondary.explanation: Being reluctant means being unwilling or hesitant.

Secondary.text: What is the antonym of "generous"?
Secondary.explanation: A selfish person keeps things for themselves, the opposite of generous.

Secondary.text: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
options: Thomas Percy, Toby, and, Emily went to Knapford.
Thomas, Percy, Toby and Emily went to Knapford.
Thomas, Percy Toby and Emily, went to Knapford.
Thomas, Percy, Toby, and, Emily went to Knapford.
Secondary.correctAnswer: Thomas, Percy, Toby and Emily went to Knapford.
Secondary.explanation: Commas separate the items in a list, with "and" before the last one.

Secondary.text: Which sentence punctuates the fronted adverbial correctly?
options: Early, in the morning Henry left the shed.
Early in the morning Henry, left the shed.
Early in, the morning Henry left the shed.
Early in the morning, Henry left the shed.
Secondary.correctAnswer: Early in the morning, Henry left the shed.
Secondary.explanation: A comma goes after the whole fronted adverbial.

Secondary.text: What is the main character in a story called?
Secondary.explanation: The protagonist is the central character of a story.

Secondary.text: In a story where Diesel keeps causing trouble for the steam engines, what is Diesel called?
Secondary.explanation: The antagonist is the character who opposes the main character.

Secondary.text: Which point of view is used in "I puffed into Tidmouth and saw Gordon waiting."?
Secondary.explanation: The narrator uses "I", so it is first person.

Secondary.text: Which word is an abstract noun?
Secondary.explanation: An abstract noun names an idea or feeling you cannot touch.

Secondary.text: Which is the correct British English spelling?
Secondary.explanation: British English doubles the "l" in "travelled".

Secondary.text: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: Percy carried: mail, parcels and milk.
Percy carried three things: mail, parcels and milk.
Percy: carried three things, mail, parcels and milk.
Percy carried three: things mail, parcels and milk.
Secondary.correctAnswer: Percy carried three things: mail, parcels and milk.
Secondary.explanation: A colon introduces a list after a complete clause.

Secondary.text: Which word is a modal verb in "Thomas might be late today."?
Secondary.explanation: "Might" is a modal verb showing possibility.

Secondary.text: Which word is a relative pronoun in "Sir Topham Hatt, who runs the railway, was pleased."?
Secondary.explanation: "Who" introduces a relative clause about Sir Topham Hatt.
